card: ROLE: Deity-figure at the center of the Shabda-Oud order; worshipped as divine authority, invoked in ritual and religious framing by the witches as their supreme power
ROLE: The living engine of the Shabda-Oud's psychic power; his brainwaves sustain the order's abilities
TRAIT: Giant golden humanoid; vast in scale; hideous and powerful in aspect; his form belongs to a category outside the human
TRAIT: Externally impenetrable to direct physical attack; no weakness at the surface; his invulnerability from outside is the established fact of his nature
TRAIT: Vulnerable only from within; his outer surface repels external force, but the interior carries no such protection
RELATIONSHIP: shabda-oud-witches (Shabda-Oud): They worship him as a deity figure and invoke him as divine authority; their psychic abilities run on his brainwaves
RELATIONSHIP: aghnar__warrior (Aghnar): An adversary who entered the Shabda-Oud domain; Jejoh engaged him directly and physically
INSTRUCTION: Treat Jejoh as an externally impenetrable psychic power-source whose apparent invulnerability depends on the outside/inside distinction
BOUNDARY: No direct speech pattern, private motive, origin, or biography is established beyond godlike Shabda-Oud authority and the witnessed confrontation with Aghnar
